notes:
Teaching gate for the kpos-shell v2 integration. Grounded directly against the shipped app, not the ux-agent proposal's own description of it: components/os/windows/inbox.tsx, report.tsx, solder.tsx, night.tsx, loadout.tsx, and darknet.tsx are ALL already real, wired, native components today, well ahead of what pipeline/proposals/ux-agent.json's notes assume is still pending. Only duel.tsx (the DIVE.EXE reskin) is unintegrated. Full reasoning for every item below lives in pipeline/gates/tutorial-review.md, this cycle's rewrite; tutorial/ledger.md carries the durable Coverage table, waiver log, and loop history.

Engine changes needed before the patchCraft items below are literal in code (stating plainly, not inventing silently): content/teaching.ts's TeachSurface union (currently tutorial | duel | day | analyze | loadout | result | upgrade | finalePre | runEnd | desktop) gains one member, 'solder'; dev/teach-sim.ts:54's WINDOW_SURFACES constant gains 'solder' alongside the existing loadout/desktop/tutorial, so the reachability walk exempts it the same way. Neither needs a new TeachWhen, a new anchor CSS rule, or a new copy order: this waiver mounts no <Teach> anywhere, it exists purely so patchCraft's firstContact can name its real surface honestly.

Biggest finding this cycle, full account in the gate and ledger: the jobBoard waiver's entire backing sentence ('Three tickets. Strain is shared across all of them. Pick your order.') is confirmed ABSENT from the shipped InboxContent, and the threatTier tip lost its list-view home (the per-ticket badge every JobBoard row used to carry) in the same collapse. teach-sim cannot see either regression, since it only checks that a waiver string exists in code and is long enough, never that the sentence it quotes still renders anywhere. One ui-spec below asks for both back.

Retired, not relocated: the patch-craft coachmark. The brief asked this gate to rule on where patch-craft's anchor should move now that crafting lives in SOLDER.BAY rather than the night screen; having read the actual shipped SolderContent (which did not exist in code when patch-craft was originally speced as PLANNED last cycle), the answer is that no anchor is needed at all. The bench's own status line states the outgrow rule verbatim on every single pickup, permanently, its Schematic panel visually blinks the gain, and its rack makes selecting an illegal partner structurally impossible, all of which is stronger, tier-0, always-on coverage that a one-shot coachmark cannot match. This also exposed a live bug the relocation framing would have quietly worked around: the coachmark currently mounts on NIGHT.SYS keyed to a craftReady signal, but the crafting UI it describes lives entirely on a different window that mounts no <Teach> at all, so a player who crafts mid-day could complete a run without ever seeing it fire.

Also resolved, overturning rather than deferring: the ux-2026-07-28-kpos-redesign gate's two-cycle-old recommendation to add a pieceDragCarry mechanic and a solder-bay-intro coachmark for SOLDER.BAY's drag gesture. Read the shipped pointer-event code directly: dragging only arms for mouse/pen (dist > 6 past pointerdown), touch always falls through to the identical tap-to-select-then-CRAFT flow every other interaction in this game already uses, and both paths resolve to the same fuseAt/rejectCancel outcomes. Nothing is reachable by drag that tap cannot also reach, so the 'new input modality nothing rewards' framing that justified the original recommendation does not hold once the fallback path is actually checked. No MECHANIC_INVENTORY entry filed. Applied the identical scrutiny to boost-swap as a control case and did NOT retire it: REPAIR.LOG's swap UI never states that CONFIGS sit outside the bay cap, a fact only the coachmark's second line carries.

Seven mechanics this cycle's audit confirmed had already silently graduated from last cycle's PLANNED status to their true TAUGHT/WAIVED state in shipped code (patchShapes, darkWebBuy, slotBuy, boostSlots, boostSwap, patchDrop, gridlockChip) and five firing-correctness asterisks confirmed clean (cascade, ram, strainChip, credits, runReset); none of these needed a proposal item, only a ledger correction, since no code or copy changes, only the record catching up to what already shipped.

Copy: no new coachmark this cycle, so no new copy order. pipeline/copy/orders/copy-patch-craft.json set to status cancelled (edited directly), superseded by the patchCraft retirement; no further words owed.

items.spec: InboxContent's collapsed list (components/os/windows/inbox.tsx), ported from inbox.html's bare-subject-line anatomy, is confirmed to drop two pieces of tier-0 coverage the old JobBoard row and header carried on every visit, permanently: (1) the header paragraph backing the jobBoard waiver ('Three tickets. Strain is shared across all of them. Pick your order.', formerly screens.tsx:211): InboxContent's kp-screen-head (lines 373-379) renders only the DAY N OF 10 hero, no subtitle. (2) a per-ticket threat-tier indicator, formerly wrapped in the threatTier TapTip on every JobBoard row (kp-job-tier, screens.tsx:234-239): the collapsed kp-inbox-item button (lines 388-399) renders only the subject string plus a CLEARED tag when done. The footer (STRAIN/RAM TapTips, credits, pouch, kit summary, lines 404-421) is confirmed intact and needs no change; do not touch it. Fix: add a paragraph stating the shared-strain fact back to InboxContent's header (verbatim or equivalent to the quoted sentence), and add a compact threat-tier indicator to each kp-inbox-item row (a right-aligned diamond-pip cluster matching the expanded CustomerCard's own THREAT TIERS row, kp-pip-row, would be visually consistent with the rest of this window), keeping it wrapped in the existing threatTier TapTip so a player can compare all three tickets' difficulty before opening any one, which the current subject-only row cannot do. Exact placement and visual form are the ux-agent's call. Worth folding into the same pass, not required for this gate: the collapsed row also dropped the per-ticket payout figure (jobPay(job.tier)), present on every JobBoard row before; nothing in the mechanic inventory gates this specifically, but it is the same class of pre-commitment comparison data as tier, and was almost certainly dropped for the same reason (porting the demo's bare anatomy, which never modeled live run data at all, rather than a deliberate cut).
acceptance: InboxContent's header shows a paragraph stating tickets are shared-strain and the pick order is the player's choice, verbatim or equivalent to today's retired JobBoard sentence, visible every time the collapsed list is shown
every collapsed kp-inbox-item row shows a threat-tier indicator, wrapped in the existing threatTier TapTip, readable without opening the ticket
the existing footer (STRAIN/RAM TapTips, CR, POUCH, KIT) is unchanged
the expanded CUSTOMER.REC card's own THREAT TIERS row and READOUT tell line are unchanged

items.spec: narrative-director's ui-copy-dive-result-overlay proposes newDiveButton ('NEW DIVE') replacing the small in-dive overlay's current single CONTINUE button (duel.tsx:918) unconditionally. duel.tsx's overlay uses that one button for all four dive outcomes today (win/core, win/gridlock, loss/severed, loss/core) via the identical finish() dispatch; relabeling all four NEW DIVE would misstate two of them: a loss (there is no new dive, the run just ended, the next screen is the run-end scene) and a win that closes the day's last ticket (the next screen is NIGHT.SYS, not a dive). Gate the label on the actual outcome: show NEW DIVE only when the result is a win AND at least one more ticket remains unclaimed that day; every other case (any loss, or a win closing the day's last ticket) keeps CONTINUE, which is accurate for all four cases today and remains the safe default. Only the label is conditional; the button's dispatch is unchanged in every case.
acceptance: on any loss (severed or core), the overlay button reads CONTINUE, never NEW DIVE
on a win that closes the day's last ticket, the overlay button reads CONTINUE, never NEW DIVE
on a win with at least one ticket still open that day, the overlay button reads NEW DIVE
the button's dispatch (finish()/onFinish) is byte-identical in every case; only the label is conditional

items.label: Combine two patch pieces into the union of their arms, at the SOLDER.BAY bench
items.rationale: Revises the existing MECHANIC_INVENTORY entry in place (id unchanged, label and firstContact updated). firstContact moves from upgrade to solder. Label drops 'at night or from the loadout bench': both are now wrong. LOADOUT.CFG's pouch panel is confirmed read-only, a button that redirects to SOLDER.BAY on click (components/os/windows/loadout.tsx:404-427, title='Open SOLDER.BAY'); NIGHT.SYS never had its own craft UI, only the coachmark that retires alongside this change (see the paired mechanic-waiver item). Paired with a mechanic-waiver item of the same id supplying the new waiver text; together they describe one revised MechanicEntry object.

items.waiver: SOLDER.BAY's own status line (components/os/windows/solder.tsx) states the outgrow rule every time a piece is picked up, before any partner is chosen: 'PICK A PARTNER. THE WELD MUST OUTGROW BOTH.' (LINE_HELD), re-stated on every single pickup for the life of the save, not once ever like a coachmark. The Schematic panel blinks exactly which arms a candidate partner would add (the arm-gain styling). The rack marks any non-outgrowing partner dead and disabled (legalPartners filtering, kp-slot-dead), so a player cannot select, drag onto, or drop a piece on an illegal partner through the shipped interface at all: the 'equal or smaller spends both pieces for nothing' risk the retiring coachmark warned about cannot actually be triggered. CRAFT carries no price anywhere in the row, matching this game's own convention that every paid action states its cost inline (NIGHT PATCH, BUY BLIND, INSTALL BOOST BAY all do), so the absence itself signals free.
items.expiresIf: the status line stops stating the outgrow rule on pickup, the dead-slot styling ever lets a non-outgrowing partner through to a live weld, or a cost is ever attached to crafting without being shown inline on the same row
items.rationale: RETIRES the patch-craft TeachingMoment (content/teaching.ts's TEACHING array) outright; the Orchestrator should delete that object, not merely edit it. Originally speced as a coachmark (deep-balance-2026-07-28, status PLANNED) against a SOLDER.BAY that did not exist in shipped code yet. The SOLDER.BAY that actually got built carries the rule at tier 0, more persistently than the moment could. This also resolves this cycle's own anchor question directly: the coachmark currently mounts on NIGHT.SYS (night.tsx:199-208) keyed to a live craftReady signal, but the entire crafting interface lives in SOLDER.BAY (solder.tsx), which mounts no <Teach> at all; a player who crafts mid-day in SOLDER.BAY, consuming the legal pair before night, could complete a run without NIGHT.SYS ever showing this coachmark. Retiring it removes a moment that was both misplaced and made redundant by superior always-on coverage, rather than relocating it to a new surface for no real gain. Engine ask this depends on: TeachSurface gains 'solder', WINDOW_SURFACES (dev/teach-sim.ts:54) gains 'solder', stated in this proposal's top-level notes. copy-patch-craft.json (pipeline/copy/orders/) set to status cancelled directly by this proposal; no further words owed on this moment.

items.waiver: LOADOUT.CFG's own program rows (components/os/windows/loadout.tsx, ProgRow) show a program's current numeric RANGE or WIDTH directly beside its TIER segment meter, for all three programs, on every visit: the widening effect this mechanic is about is the two numbers sitting next to each other, not a sentence describing it.
items.expiresIf: a program row ever shows a TIER meter without its RANGE/WIDTH value in the same row, or the shown number stops changing when a tier upgrades
items.rationale: Re-citation, not a new waiver, and the mechanic stays WAIVED throughout. The prior citation (the old KitScreen header at screens.tsx:359-364, 'tiers come from closed days...') no longer exists anywhere in the shipped surface: LOADOUT.CFG's redesign (components/os/windows/loadout.tsx, integrated ahead of this cycle's own gate) replaced that header with a DIVE KIT status readout that does not restate it in prose, confirmed by direct read this cycle. The replacement citation is stronger, not merely adequate: LOADOUT.CFG's ProgRow already shows the concrete number (RANGE for SCAN, WIDTH for ATTACK/DEFEND) directly beside the TIER meter, demonstrating the exact fact this mechanic cares about (a tier number correlates with a bigger output number) more concretely than the retired prose sentence ever stated it. dayUpgrade (a separate, independently-taught mechanic, coachmark day-upgrade) already covers where a tier increase comes from procedurally; this waiver is narrowly about the widening effect itself, which is now shown, not told. kitConfig, the sibling mechanic the old header also backed, is unaffected: it was never a pure-waiver claim (see tutorial/ledger.md, 'kitConfig: NOT a waiver'), and its own basis, the modeLocked tip, is confirmed still live on every locked mode button in ProgRow's tipFor.

items.waiver: Holds only while INBOX's collapsed ticket list carries a permanent paragraph stating tickets are shared-strain and the order is the player's choice, somewhere on the window (exact position unspecified). Audit 2026-07-29 found this paragraph confirmed ABSENT from the shipped InboxContent (components/os/windows/inbox.tsx): the collapsed view's kp-screen-head shows only the DAY N OF 10 hero, no subtitle anywhere. ui-spec inbox-collapsed-row-parity (this proposal) asks for it back; re-widen this waiver to the unconditional form once that lands and is confirmed directly against the live component, not assumed from the proposal.
items.expiresIf: restated for emphasis: the backing sentence is confirmed absent from INBOX today. This waiver does not currently hold. Re-check is owed the moment inbox-collapsed-row-parity is reported integrated, by reading the component, the same way this finding was made.
items.rationale: Narrows the existing waiver, on the exact precedent the credits waiver already set in 2026-07-26 ('narrowed... the full-sweep audit found the crack the original entry predicted'). The underlying claim broke when JobBoard was absorbed into INBOX without the sentence explicitly carrying forward; teach-sim cannot catch this class of break, since it only checks that the waiver string exists in code and is long enough, never that the English sentence it quotes still renders anywhere on the actual screen. This is the most severe finding of this cycle's audit for exactly that reason: the harness stayed green the entire time this was broken.
